subject: Tenant Drillpad delivery & observability questions
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-07-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Tenant Drillpad delivery & observability questions

Hi team,

Quick ask: leadership has asked for a lightweight "Tenant Drillpad" for the Console that lets CS and sales quickly surface per-tenant cost and tail-latency breakdowns during demos (GreenWave Health demo penciled for 2029-07-26). We don't need full forensic tooling in time, but we do need a clear answer on feasibility and a small canary-able surface.

I wrote a very short PRD (attached) with suggested scope — three views: summary (cost + P95/P99), per-route breakdown (model and route contributions), and a small trace list (sampled). Can each of you reply with the following by EOD tomorrow?
- Marissa: minimal backend metrics/queries we can reuse and expected query cost impact (rough ballpark).
- Karthik: retention/sampling policy constraints, data privacy concerns (token traces), and a rough effort estimate for a safe canary rollout.
- Sofia: quick UX placement recommendation and a tiny list of default columns/filters that will be most useful for demos.

Attachment: tenant-drillpad-prd.md (text/markdown)

Goal: internal canary ready by 2029-07-22, demo-ready but behind a feature flag 2029-07-26. If anything here is unrealistic, call it out and propose a smaller first cut.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Sr. Product Manager, Console & Observability
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-07-11T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant Drillpad delivery & observability questions

Lauren — thanks, this is clear and doable as a scoped MVP. Quick notes:

What we can reuse today:
- Existing aggregated time-series (1m granularity) we already compute per-tenant: requests, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_p50/p95/p99.
- Per-route/topology cardinality breakdown is available if we pre-aggregate by (tenant, route, model).

Suggested minimal endpoints:
- /api/console/tenants/:id/drillpad/summary (1m aggregated window, last 7 days by default)
- /api/console/tenants/:id/drillpad/routes (top N routes with cost breakdown)
- /api/console/tenants/:id/drillpad/samples (sampled traces; sampling policy required)

Estimated incremental cost: modest for low-query volume — if we compute on read with 1m rollups it's cheap. I'll attach a query example and a ballpark compute estimate (see query-sample.sql).

Open items for Karthik:
- Sampling rate we can expose for the samples endpoint without exposing PII.
- Retention defaults for high-resolution data.

I'll own the backend contract and can deliver a first-pass read-only API in 1 sprint if Karthik can support data prep.

Marissa Cole
Analytics & Observability PM
Redwood Inference
Attachment: query-sample.sql (text/sql)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-07-11T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant Drillpad delivery & observability questions

Thanks — couple of guardrails and feasibility notes: 

1) High-cardinality tenants: computing per-tenant, per-route, per-model rollups on the fly risks hot partitions for large customers. We should do incremental pre-aggregation (minute buckets) into a read-optimized store. That avoids per-request scan cost.

2) Sampling & PII: we cannot show token-level content in the samples list for customers who opt-out or have sensitive data. We can surface trace metadata (prompt hash, token_count, latency, model) and an option for redacted snippets. Token-level traces should be gated behind explicit customer consent and SOC2 review.

3) Retention: for demo purposes 7 days high-res (1m), 30 days low-res (hourly) is reasonable. If Sales wants longer retention we need a cost + approval path. See attached quick storage estimate.

4) Effort: backend/data-prep: ~2 sprints (2 infra + 2 analytics engineers) for the pre-aggregation + read API + feature flag. UI: ~1 sprint (Sofia) for the initial surface. QA + canary rollout: add 1 sprint. So total ~4 sprints end-to-end non-blocking but can be split into a demoable first cut in 2 sprints by limiting rows and retention.

5) Canary plan suggestion: 1) internal-only flag for Redwood org, 2) small set of beta customers (CS-run), 3) circuit-breaker rate limits per tenant for read paths.

I'll open SUP-1428 for infra work and paste a short cost file (storage-cost-estimate.csv). Need Marissa to confirm exact query shapes so we can size.

Karthik Iyer
Engineering Manager, Data & Platform
Redwood Inference

Quick UX sketch notes:

Placement:
- Add a new "Tenant Drillpad" tab inside the existing Tenant detail page (next to Activity / Settings). That's where CS expects it during calls.

Default view (collapsed):
- Header: tenant name, billing tier, feature-flag status
- Summary cards: 24h cost, 7d cost trend, P95 latency (7d), error rate (7d)
- Route table (top 10 by cost): columns = route, model, calls, tokens_out, pct_cost, p95_latency; actions: open samples, open time-series.

Samples panel:
- Show sampled traces metadata only (redacted snippet toggle). Link to full Trace UI for customers who have consent.

Mobile not a priority for this first cut. I'll put a tight Figma mock here: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz/Tenant-Drillpad-Mockup.

Deliverables I can ship in 1 sprint for the demo: small mock + component spec + accessibility notes.

Sofia Ivanova
Product Designer, Console UX
Redwood Inference
